notes.text: In Act 1, we discovered how generalization / base class works. Several different things can share the same core traits. When they do, we group them under one shared label. In Python, that label becomes a class, the foundation every member builds on.

In Act 2, we discovered how child class / is-a relationship works. A child keeps every trait of the shared group automatically. Then it adds its own special ability on top. In Python, class Eagle(Animal): says “Eagle IS-A Animal”.

In Act 1, we discovered how generalization / base class works. Several different things can share the same core traits. When they do, we group them under one shared label. In Python, that label becomes a class, the foundation every member builds on.

In Act 2, we discovered how child class / is-a relationship works. A child keeps every trait of the shared group automatically. Then it adds its own special ability on top. In Python, class Eagle(Animal): says “Eagle IS-A Animal”.

In Act 3, we discovered how the name: inheritance works. When one type automatically receives all the traits of another and adds its own, it is called Inheritance. Animal is the parent, Eagle is the child. Parent = shared foundation. Child = foundation + its own additions.

In Act 4, we discovered how class eagle(animal): in python works. class Eagle(Animal): means Eagle is a specialization of Animal. The parent class holds the shared traits. The eagle automatically gets everything Animal defines, and adds its own fly().
